title: Add per-chunk content digests for partial verification

state.decision_rationale: Deferred until independent partial retrieval, caching, or retransmission exists. Whole-file plus envelope integrity is sufficient today; repeated high-entropy hashes are unjustified without a consumer.

provenance.source_label: Claude Fable feature idea: per-chunk hashes
provenance.review_target: Reported 39479-line MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Per-chunk digests enable partial verification and partial retransmission; currently integrity is only file-level.
feedback.normalized_claim: Bind each exact chunk to its own content digest so consumers can verify, cache, retrieve, or retransmit chunks independently.

current_behavior: The index contains one full digest per source file, and the parser verifies the concatenated chunk content against it.
Chunk terminators contain a prefix of the file digest, not a digest of the individual chunk.
Chunk records carry byte counts and ranges but no chunk content identity.
Adaptive or analyzer-dependent chunk boundaries would make chunk identities less stable across generator changes.

proposal.summary: Evaluate full per-chunk digests or a Merkleized content structure when partial verification and retrieval are actual supported workflows, rather than adding repeated entropy solely for appearance.
candidate_changes: Define a chunk digest over exact payload bytes and include it once in chunk metadata or a compact digest table.
Specify how ordered chunk digests reconstruct and bind the source-file digest.
Support selective chunk verification with proof of membership if a Merkle design is chosen.
Measure digest token overhead against partial-transfer and cache benefits.
non_goals: Do not describe the current digest-prefixed terminator as a per-chunk hash.
Do not remove the authoritative whole-file digest.
Do not add high-entropy fields without a consumer workflow that uses them.

questions: Will consumers retrieve chunks independently or always receive complete files?
Should chunk identity depend on line boundaries, byte ranges, or content alone?
Is a flat digest list sufficient, or is a Merkle proof needed?
risks: Full digests add substantial token cost across hundreds of chunks.
Chunk-boundary changes destroy cache identity despite unchanged file bytes.
Partial verification can be misunderstood as proof of complete-file availability.
evidence_needed: Partial retrieval and retransmission prototype measurements.
Token-cost comparison for full, truncated, tabled, and Merkle digests.
Verification tests for reordered, duplicated, omitted, and substituted chunks.
